alignments.note: Rule 51's anarthrous clause: the supplied indefinite is a helper on the noun.
Rule 17: of + noun heads on the noun; the supplied the is a helper, the Greek being anarthrous.
Rule 106: the preverb ἐπι- is realized by by, no Greek preposition being expressed; the supplied object him is a rule 7 pronoun helper. Head on the verb word stood.

Rule 106's accusative arm: τὴν πλευράν is the accusative object and an accusative has no case for an English preposition to realize, so the on of the recast smote Peter on the side is the verb's own government and stays inside its unit, discontinuously under rule 15.
Name; the ASV's recast makes it the verb's object and writes no of for the genitive.
Bare noun, the on belonging to the verb under rule 106.
Rule 88: the supplied juncture and is a helper on the finite verb it introduces.
Rule 106: the preverb ἀνα- is realized by up; head on the verb word Rise.

Corrected: ἐν τάχει is one unit. Rule 94's precondition is met, the phrase rendering to the single English word quickly, and rule 39's test keeps the unit aligned rather than noncompositional, part of the English answering to the governed noun's own lexeme; headed on that noun, as 1TI.3.14, REV.1.1, ROM.16.20 and LUK.18.8 all head their single word on τάχει. The earlier reading left ἐν unrepresented under rule 34, but rule 93's test asks what the corpus spends on the governed word: τάχος is a noun, quickly and shortly are what the corpus spends on the cognate adverb ταχέως, and a noun does not spell an English adverb by itself, the adverbial force being the preposition's and the dative's. No corpus unit leaves this ἐν unrepresented. Reading the pair as noncompositional remains the competing analysis and is refused for the reason rule 45 gives, that some part of the English answers to a source token.
Genitive pronoun rendered by the possessive his.
Rule 20: αὐτοῦ occupies the determiner slot, so the article realizes nothing.
Rule 106's addition arm: the ASV writes off for the preverb ἐκ- in addition to the complete from for the expressed ἐκ, so each token takes its own and the verb does not go bare.
Rule 36: the expressed preposition takes from.
Rule 20 second arm: no possessor token stands in this phrase, αὐτοῦ having been spent on the first his under rule 76's availability test, so the supplied his is the article's own.

review_notes: Corrected: ἐν and τάχει are now one aligned unit on quickly, headed on τάχει, following the corpus unanimously (1TI.3.14, REV.1.1, ROM.16.20, LUK.18.8). The noncompositional reading remains the alternative and is refused under rule 45's test.
The BSB disagreement on this ἐν is therefore a genuine error corrected, not a convention difference.

Everything else in the verse stands as accepted: on at t022 inside πατάξας's unit under rule 106's accusative arm, and off plus from divided between preverb and expressed preposition under rule 106's addition arm.
